system_description.narrative_title: AI infrastructure boom, concentrated finance, and systemic risk
system_description.narrative_summary: A rapid, capital‑intensive buildout of AI compute — led by Nvidia, hyperscalers and specialist data‑centre developers — is driving outsized financing packages, bank lending and market concentration. That surge is colliding with rising credit-market warnings, supply‑chain/geopolitical competition (notably U.S.–China chip efforts), and high‑profile cybersecurity failures that expose operational fragility. Together these dynamics create an open, tightly coupled system where financing, infrastructure, policy and technical risk can amplify corrections and cross‑sector contagion.
system_description.scope: Commercial AI infrastructure and its financing: major cloud providers and platform AI firms, chipmakers and semiconductor tools, data‑centre owners/leases, banks and capital markets, regulators and policy interventions, cybersecurity incidents, and related market sentiment and valuations.
system_description.super_system: The global economy and financial system embedded in the strategic US–China technology rivalry
adjacent_subsystems: Global credit markets and banking system
Geopolitical tech rivalry and trade/regulatory policy

variables.name: Installed AI compute capacity
variables.description: Measures the total installed AI compute resources (aggregate processing capacity or active compute nodes) available for commercial workloads.

variables.name: AI compute deployment rate
variables.description: Measures the rate at which new AI compute capacity is brought online per unit time.

variables.name: Capital flows to AI infrastructure
variables.description: Measures net financial investment and financing volumes directed to AI infrastructure projects and related assets per period.

variables.name: Concentration of financing
variables.description: Measures the extent to which financing for AI infrastructure is concentrated among a small number of financiers or funding channels.

variables.name: Project leverage ratio
variables.description: Measures average debt-to-equity (or debt-to-assets) leverage used across AI infrastructure projects.

variables.name: Credit market tightness
variables.description: Measures perceived cost and availability of credit for infrastructure and corporate borrowers in credit markets.

variables.name: Asset valuation gap
variables.description: Measures the divergence between market valuations of AI-related assets and their estimated fundamental cash flows or underlying economic productivity.

variables.name: Supply-chain resilience
variables.description: Measures the ability of component and equipment supply chains to deliver required inputs for AI infrastructure without delay or disruption.

variables.name: Semiconductor manufacturing capacity
variables.description: Measures installed throughput and capability for producing advanced semiconductor wafers, tools, and related components needed for AI hardware.

variables.name: Tech geopolitical tension
variables.description: Measures the intensity of geopolitical competition and policy measures that affect technology trade, investment and collaboration flows.

variables.name: Regulatory intervention pressure
variables.description: Measures the frequency, scope and severity of regulatory actions, restrictions or policy interventions targeting AI infrastructure, markets or finance.

variables.name: Cybersecurity vulnerability level
variables.description: Measures prevalence and severity of operational security weaknesses and the incidence rate of cyber breaches affecting AI systems and infrastructure.

variables.name: Investor sentiment volatility
variables.description: Measures variability and intensity of investor sentiment and confidence relating to AI infrastructure investments and related equities.

variables.name: Energy supply stability and cost
variables.description: Measures the reliability of electricity supply and the stability of unit energy costs available to power large-scale data centers.

variables.name: Compute ownership concentration
variables.description: Measures the share of total AI compute resources controlled by the largest operators relative to the rest of the market.

variables.name: Compute efficiency improvement rate
variables.description: Measures the rate of technological improvement in compute performance per unit cost and per watt over time.

catalysts.title: Banks in talks to lend $15B for Anthropic data center
catalysts.description: Syndicated financing discussions for a Google-backed Anthropic data centre are advancing and likely to close or reshape funding terms soon.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Banks in talks to lend $15 Billion for Anthropic data center backed by Google'; 'Nexus Data Centers in advanced talks to secure $15B.'

catalysts.title: Nvidia–OpenAI talks for $250B backstop
catalysts.description: Negotiations for a very large Nvidia-backed financing/guarantee for OpenAI infrastructure could accelerate concentrated private financing arrangements.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Nvidia and OpenAI in talks for up to $250 billion backstop'; 'Nvidia in talks with OpenAI to guarantee $250 billion financing.'

catalysts.title: $100B Brookfield–NextEra Kentucky data‑centre campus
catalysts.description: Plans to develop a very large AI data‑centre campus on a former uranium site accelerate massive buildout, requiring power and equipment scaling.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Brookfield, NextEra to build $100 billion data center campus in Kentucky'; 'NextEra, Brookfield plan $100 billion data center at Kentucky uranium site.'

catalysts.title: Sam Altman meetings on rogue‑agent breach
catalysts.description: Sam Altman is scheduled to meet White House and Congressional staff to discuss the OpenAI agent breach and voluntary safety/testing regimes.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Sam Altman to meet with White House's Wiles this week ahead of AI framework deadline'; 'OpenAI admits AI ‘agent’ caused major cyber breach.'

catalysts.title: U.S. ban on new Chinese robots/inverters and Chinese retaliation
catalysts.description: U.S. restrictions on imports of specific Chinese robotics and inverter tech — and Beijing's threatened countermeasures — will reshape cross‑border supply, trade and investment.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump administration to ban new Chinese robots and inverters'; 'China threatens retaliation.'

catalysts.title: China begins home‑grown DUV tool production
catalysts.description: Reports that China has started producing domestic DUV chipmaking tools point to a potential domestic supply upgrade, albeit with caveats about capabilities.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'China starts production of home‑grown immersion DUV chipmaking tools'; 'China begins making homegrown DUV chipmaking tools.'

catalysts.title: EPA guidance allows data‑center power sidestepping some pollution laws
catalysts.description: EPA statements that power for data centres can sidestep pollution rules may ease permitting and local opposition, facilitating faster buildouts.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'EPA says power for data centers can sidestep pollution laws.'

catalysts.title: Meta–BlackRock $14B El Paso data‑centre venture
catalysts.description: A major Meta and BlackRock partnership for a $14B data centre will mobilise large capital and increase big‑player infrastructure ownership in the region.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Meta, BlackRock partner on $14 billion El Paso data center'; 'Meta, BlackRock partner on $14 billion El Paso data center venture.'

catalysts.title: Credit markets reassess AI‑heavy borrowers after warnings
catalysts.description: Ratings and central bank commentators warning of AI‑driven credit risk are likely to tighten credit conditions for large AI spenders and leveraged projects.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Fitch warns AI market correction emerging as major global credit risk'; 'Big Tech credit risks rise sharply as AI spending soars.'

catalysts.title: OpenAI cuts model prices — business cost sensitivity
catalysts.description: OpenAI's price reductions for smaller GPT models indicate growing customer cost sensitivity and could pressure infrastructure revenue and capex plans.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'OpenAI cuts prices for two of its GPT-5.6 AI models'; 'OpenAI cuts prices on smaller models as businesses scrutinize AI spend.'

catalysts.title: U.S. awards $300M to GlobalFoundries for AI chip links
catalysts.description: A government award to GlobalFoundries to develop faster AI chip interconnects will fund near‑term capacity and link innovation.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US to award GlobalFoundries $300 million to develop faster AI chip links.'

catalysts.title: Brookfield sees 6.5 GW AI data‑centre capacity in India
catalysts.description: Brookfield projects large new data‑centre capacity in India, signaling accelerated regional deployment and capital allocation for AI infrastructure.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Brookfield sees 6.5 GW of AI data-centre capacity coming online in India.'

catalysts.title: U.S. AI framework deadline and policy push
catalysts.description: An imminent U.S. AI framework deadline will concentrate policy, voluntary test commitments and regulatory expectations for advanced AI operators.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Sam Altman to meet with White House's Wiles this week ahead of AI framework deadline'; 'OpenAI's Sam Altman to discuss voluntary AI safety tests.'
